note: WHY s.el WRAPS IT IN `save-match-data', frozen as a value. `count-matches' searches, so it leaves the match register on its LAST match: Emacs answers (2 4 6), the 4..6 being the second `an' in the buffer, which has replaced the (0 3) the `string-match' before it left. So a kg `count-matches' is not required to preserve the register -- it is required to clobber it exactly this way -- and s.el's own `save-match-data' around the call is what makes `s-count-matches' side-effect-free anyway. kg answered `void-function' before 26.2 and answers (2 4 6) now -- clobbered exactly this way, which is a requirement and not an accident.
